question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is '**useless**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The passage describes water rushing into the ship "not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet." This indicates widespread damage across multiple compartments.
 
• The steel doors were designed to contain water in separate compartments (watertight compartments). However, if the damage spanned "hundred feet" and affected "separate places," these doors would be ineffective in stopping the overall inflow of water.
 
• Therefore, the steel doors, meant to prevent widespread flooding, became "**useless**" (बेकार) in the face of such extensive damage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

Complete Passage: *The ship struck the iceberg (1) **with **__its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2) __**moments**__, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)__useless__. Captain Smith soon understood that (4)______ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1: "painted"** – "Painted" (रंगा हुआ) has no relevance to the functionality of the doors in preventing flooding.
 
• **Option 3: "burnt"** – There is no mention of fire in the passage; the damage is from water ingress.
 
• **Option 4: "complete"** – "Complete" (पूरा) would imply they were intact and functional, which contradicts the context of the ship sinking due to extensive damage.
